messages:
anna (privacy): FYI: received a DSAR (erasure) for account u-3b7. Primary DB rows purged yesterday. Concern: archived embeddings + logs in cold storage across regions. Need clear plan to show we've taken reasonable steps.

sasha (sec-eng): thanks. two quick asks: 1) can infra prove which backups contain the user id (not just a full-restore) 2) any KMS/HSM constraints (imported key material, key-destruction policies) that would block selective deletion?

mike (infra): backup index has per-object metadata but sometimes missing for older snapshots pre-2025. backups encrypted with CMEK hosted in our HSM-backed KMS. note: key versions v1..v3 exist; we imported v1 (external material) for a migration — destroying v1 isn't possible without special approval.

lou (oncall): also flag: `restore-agent` SA still has broad kms.decrypt. adding to rotation checklist.

anna (privacy): if we can't remove targeted blobs due to imported material, we'll need to open a retention-exception + document mitigations. legal sign-off required before any key destruction.

kate (legal): correct. destruction of an HSM-imported key is risky and likely disproportionate. prefer targeted removal where possible, with a formal manifest and audit trail. we can approve retention-exception if we have a clear business/legal rationale and compensating controls.

sasha (sec-eng): Proposed technical flow: 1) run fingerprint scan over archives for markers (user id patterns, hashed email) 2) create list-of-objects manifest -> store in `gs://privacy-manifests/u-3b7/` 3) attempt per-object re-encryption to a quarantine key we control, then delete original object 4) if re-encryption fails due to key policy, mark for retention-exception. All actions logged to audit cluster.

mike (infra): quick proof-of-concept command to pull object metadata (fast):

```
gsutil ls -L gs://redwood-archives/2025-* | grep -A2 "Metadata: userids" | grep "u-3b7"
```

and to re-encrypt an object we can run a server-side copy with new CMEK: `gsutil rewrite -k projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/privacy/cryptoKeys/quarantine-key gs://bucket/object`

rotation-bot: scheduled key-rotation for `legacy-restore-sa` on 2026-03-05 04:00 UTC. :rotating_light:

sasha (sec-eng): RBAC change: create `groups@redwood.org` group `privacy-deleters` and a narrow `roles/privacy.scanner` IAM role with `storage.objects.get` & `storage.objects.delete` limited to `projects/_/buckets/redwood-archives/objects/privacy/*`. Will open PR and add infra/privacy/legal reviewers. Audit logs enabled for all deletions.

lou (oncall): vuln note: found an old restore process that caches decrypted objects for 48h in `/var/tmp/restore-cache` on restore workers. need to add secure-delete step pre- and post-restore. filing infra ticket.

anna (privacy): timeline: run scan by EOD, publish manifest, try re-encrypt/delete. If blocked, we'll open retention-exception (ticket PRIV-3219) with docs, mitigations (access reduction, key rotation plan) and an ETA. Kate, can legal draft exception wording?

kate (legal): will draft. include the scan evidence and why destruction is disproportionate. also request mitigation deadlines.

sasha (sec-eng): will push IAM PR + audit pipeline changes. ping when manifest available.

mike (infra): scan complete: found 5 objects referencing u-3b7 across 3 snapshots (eu-west-1, us-central1). re-encrypt attempt succeeded for 4 objects, one failed due to imported key v1. added to PRIV-3219. moving deleted objects to `quarantine` then issuing secure wipe.
